what_its_for: Selegiline is used to treat Parkinson's disease. It helps control symptoms like tremors, stiffness, and slow movement. The skin patch form (Emsam) is also used to treat depression. It works by increasing certain brain chemicals that help nerve cells communicate properly.
how_to_take: Selegiline comes in different forms. TABLETS or CAPSULES: Swallow whole with a full glass of water. Take with breakfast and lunch — do NOT take in the evening or at night because it may keep you awake. ORALLY DISINTEGRATING TABLETS (Zelapar): Do NOT eat or drink for 5 minutes before and after taking this tablet. Place the tablet on top of your tongue and let it dissolve completely — do not swallow it whole or chew it. SKIN PATCH (Emsam): Apply to dry, clean skin on your upper chest, upper arm, or upper thigh. Rotate the location each day. Wear only ONE patch at a time. Change the patch every 24 hours at the same time each day. Press firmly for 30 seconds to make sure it sticks.
dosing: Your doctor will tell you the exact dose that is right for you. TABLETS/CAPSULES: The usual dose is 5 mg taken twice a day — once at breakfast and once at lunch. Never take more than 10 mg per day. ORALLY DISINTEGRATING TABLETS: Usually 1.25 mg once a day in the morning. Your doctor may increase this to 2.5 mg after 6 weeks if needed. SKIN PATCH: Doses range from 6 mg/24 hours up to 12 mg/24 hours depending on what your doctor prescribes. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if it is still morning or early afternoon. If it is late afternoon or evening, skip the missed dose and take your next dose as scheduled the next morning. NEVER take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. For the skin patch, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next patch change, skip the missed one and continue your regular schedule.
storage: Store tablets and capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do NOT store in the bathroom. Keep the orally disintegrating tablets in their original packaging and only remove one tablet right before you use it. For the skin patch, store at room temperature and keep patches in their sealed pouches until ready to use. After removing a used patch, fold it in half with the sticky sides together and safely dispose of it in the trash — away from children and pets. Keep ALL forms of this medication out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: FOODS TO AVOID with higher doses (above 10 mg tablets/capsules or above 6 mg patch): Avoid foods high in tyramine, which can cause a dangerous spike in blood pressure. These include aged cheeses (cheddar, parmesan, brie), cured or smoked meats (salami, pepperoni, hot dogs), pickled or fermented foods, sauerkraut, soy sauce, tap beer, red wine, and overripe or dried fruits. Ask your pharmacist or doctor for a full tyramine food list. MEDICATIONS TO AVOID: Do NOT take antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics), tramadol, meperidine (Demerol), methadone, dextromethorphan (found in many cough medicines), or other MAO inhibitors. Always tell every doctor, dentist, and pharmacist you see that you take selegiline before starting any new medication. ACTIVITIES: Be careful driving or using heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you. It may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Avoid alcohol. Avoid suddenly stopping this medication without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: A sudden, severe headache (this could be a sign of dangerously high blood pressure), chest pain, rapid or irregular heartbeat, stiff neck, nausea and vomiting, sweating, or vision changes. Also contact your doctor if you notice: New or worsening depression, unusual thoughts, hallucinations, or thoughts of hurting yourself. Uncontrollable urges such as gambling, eating, or sexual behavior (this can be a rare side effect). Severe skin reaction where the patch is applied. Signs of a serious drug interaction such as confusion, agitation, rapid heart rate, muscle twitching, or high fever. Call your doctor for regular check-ins about how the medication is working and any side effects you may be experiencing.
when_it_works: For Parkinson's disease, you may start to notice some improvement in your symptoms within a few days to a few weeks, but it may take up to 4 to 6 weeks to feel the full benefit. For depression (skin patch), it may take 2 to 4 weeks to start feeling better, and up to 6 to 8 weeks for full improvement. Keep taking your medication even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The safety of selegiline during pregnancy is not fully known. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. BREASTFEEDING: It is not known if selegiline passes into breast milk. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication without first talking to your doctor. ELDERLY PATIENTS: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness, falls, confusion, and hallucinations. Use with extra caution and report any unusual symptoms to your doctor right away. CHILDREN: Selegiline is generally not recommended for children. Safety and effectiveness in children have not been well established. KIDNEY or LIVER PROBLEMS: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted or selegiline may not be right for you.
